title: High Volatility and Action Bias Distinguish LLMs from Humans in Group Coordination
abstract: arXiv:2604.02578v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Humans exhibit remarkable abilities to coordinate in groups. As large language models (LLMs) become more capable, it remains an open question whether they can demonstrate comparable adaptive coordination and whether they use the same strategies as humans. To better understand this, we compare LLM and human performance on a common-interest game with imperfect monitoring: Group Binary Search. In this $n$-player game, participants need to coordinate their actions to achieve a common objective. Players independently submit numerical values in an effort to collectively sum to a randomly assigned target number. Without direct communication, they rely on group feedback to iteratively adjust their submissions until they reach the target number. Our findings show that, unlike humans who adapt and stabilize their behavior over time, LLMs often fail to improve across games and exhibit excessive switching, which impairs group convergence.

translated_title: 高波动性与行动偏差使大语言模型在群体协调中区别于人类
translated_abstract: 人类在群体协调方面展现出非凡的能力。随着大语言模型（LLMs）能力的不断提升，它们能否表现出与人类相当的适应性协调能力，以及它们是否采用与人类相同的策略，仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。为了更好地理解这一点，我们在一个具有不完美监督的共同利益博弈——群体二分搜索中比较了大语言模型与人类的表现。在这个n人博弈中，参与者需要协调各自的行动以实现共同目标。玩家独立提交数值，力求使所有数值之和等于一个随机指定的目标数字。在没有直接沟通的情况下，他们依靠群体反馈来迭代调整自己的提交，直到达到目标数字。我们的研究结果表明，与人类会随时间适应并稳定其行为不同，大语言模型往往无法在多轮博弈中取得进步，并表现出过度的策略切换，这损害了群体的收敛。
tldr: 通过群体二分搜索博弈对比发现，大语言模型在群体协调任务中表现出高波动性和行动偏差，无法像人类那样随时间适应并稳定行为，其过度的策略切换阻碍了群体收敛。
en_tdlr: Comparing LLMs and humans in a Group Binary Search game reveals that LLMs exhibit high volatility and action bias, failing to adapt and stabilize their behavior over time like humans, with excessive switching impairing group convergence.
